title.narrative: AWESOME(Advancing Women's Engagement: Strengthening Opportunities to Mobilise for Equality)

description.narrative: A 5 year advocacy programme to support women's movements in Ethiopia,Kenya and Uganda to be strengthened, less, fragmented and more representative of diverse groups of women, including women with disabilities. These stronger women's movements will contribute to strong women leaders at all levels and the prevention and elimination of sexual and gender based violence (SGBV)

activity-date.narrative: No new women were reached during the reporting period. During the WRO conference, we held a pre conference feedback and evaluation conference to investigate successes and gather feedback and conduct a deepdive into the current state of women's rights in the different counties. From the survey, 94% of the partcipants shared that the conference was relevant and addressed the current discourse and provided a platform for networking. Recommendations on where FIDA-Kenya can improve were also provided. A joint communique was also developed at the end of the conference with demands to duty bearers on the femicide crisis in Kenya.

comment.narrative: There is a 50% implementation of existing SGBV laws and policies on women's rights. FIDA will measure the increase in implementation through the number of advocacy effors each year, for which the baseline is 0.Our baseline found slow uptake of the SGBV legislative framework. In terms of what has already been done to support the cause, there have been consultative/ lobby meetings, policy dialogues with duty bearers and submissions of memos."
we had target 2 advocacy actions each year

This is 2 advocacy effors in year 1 and 2 in year 2.Year 1: Gender policy 2021 Anti-FGM declaration 2021In Year 2:2 advocacy efforts were conducted in Year 2 which included 2 consultative meetings with the Judiciary through NCAJ on SOA and GBV engagements. 4 other advocacy efforts with Garissa mediation council, Nairobi County Gender Department High-Level Discussion on Women Political Participation, and 7 community awareness forums. A memorandum on disabilty friendly spaces was issued to the county government of Mombasa after a peaceful procession was done at bima towers, county assembly and governor’s office.FIDA-Kenya has facilitated 2 meetings of the NCAJ to review the sexual offences ACT . The committee is in the progress of identifying key sections of the SOA such as prohibition of plea bargaining and expounding on forms of sexual harassment. Further, criminalization of initiating or conniving to conceal a sexual offence.FIDA-K Participated in a conference in Banjul where a joint statement was developed and issued

description.narrative: Self outcome 1.04: Number of representatives (of women’s rights orgs) in each regional who are actively participating in the network and report feeling safe and included by the WRMs

comment.narrative: "WROs from across the regions of Kenya are not currently adequately included in the nationwide movement. This indicator will target 160 representatives from 80 WROs (who are involved in 8 regional forums, bringing together 10 WROs in each region of Nairobi, Nakuru, Garissa, Embu, Nyeri, Kakamega, Kisumu and Mombasa). These same individuals will be worked with during the 5 years of AWESOME."

By the end of AWESOME, the desired change is that 160 representatives are actively participating in their network, and report feeling safe and included with the women's rights movement (meaning WROs and community groups). Actively participating means regularly attending meetings.

113 women attended 7 regional forums where their skills on Advocacy on gender issues were enhanced. A National WROs conference was also held later on in December recording a total of 22 women whose skills in movement building and legal provisions regarding Gender matters were sharped. later in the month, A total of 67 Women leaders held a National dialogue on women leadership and feminism.The difference of 78 could be reduced if an 8th regional forum could have been held. over 500 women were however reached through community forums, and Legal aid .Tough no new women are reported, we continue to engage with the 80 that we initially had in 2021 The content of the capacity building initiatives- 7 WRO regional forums and 1 LSK breakfast meeting was held in the year. The trainings brought together all the 35 WROs in the regions with the aim of enhancing their capacity and effectiveness in advancing gender equality and eliminating GBV, facilitate knowledge sharing among the WROs and to foster unity in advancing policy and legal reforms that promote women’s rights, gender equality and women empowerment at the county and national levels.- The changes in knowledge & skills-women have embraced feminism and are using it to fight patriarchy and social norms that promote SGBV. There is increased referrals for legal aid interventions and enhanced collaboration among the WROs in coordinating strategies and undertaking advocacy for women’s rights at the county level . There is also increased knowledge among the WROs having been trained on various topical issues among them legal frameworks on SGBV, human rights-based approaches in handling survivors of SGBV, leadership and governance, significance of women’s participation in leadership and effective advocacy for good governance, policy and legislative reforms. - Which measure is used to assess the capacity of the individuals? The content of the capacity building initiatives: The forums brought together 80 WROs and 320 participants from the 8 provinces of Kenya. Participants were trained on feminism and feministic approaches. Mentors also participated in learning and experience sharing lessons. The WROs were selected based on their record of work on women’s leadership and participation and their work on the elimination of SGBV. The forums were intended for capacity building and creation of collaborative advocacy platforms to ensure accountability of duty bearers to commitments made on women’s leadership and the elimination of SGBV.
